text:
Introduction
This document outlines the hydraulic oil filling procedures I1, which
must be performed every two years as indicated by Y2 in the title block, This procedure should be carried out when:
 - Cleaning or changing the oil filter.
 - Changing the pump hose.
 - Repairing or changing the pressure relief valve (14.37).
Safety Precautions
A work permit must be issued, 
qualified maintenance staff carry the suitable safety ID category
Safety fence (rope) with caution 
marks surrounding the work area,
Wear your safety helmet, shoes .... etc.
Breaker must be isolated.
Control power disconnected.
Tools and Equipment
Tools: Normal Tools
Material: Oil Type Aeroshell Fluid # 4, Rags
Work to be carried out
Note: Refer to the attached drawings. Figures no. 1 & 2 .
Unscrew cap (14.3. 1) from the filler of the oil reservoir
Take out the venting screws (14.12)
Open the pressure equalizing valve (14.37) in the control unit
Pour new hydraulic oil into the oil reservoir. Use only Aero Shell Fluid
 (4), do not substitute any other oil.
Take extreme care to see that no foreign matter (dust, sand) enters the
 hydraulic system. Fill the oil in slowly to avoid air bubbles entering the
 system.
To fill the high pressure side of the hydraulic system, start the oil pump
 and stop it soon as the oil comes out of the vents on the operating
 mechanism
Refit the venting screws (14.12) and screw them tight
Again add oil to the reservoir up to the level in step 5
Refit cap (14.3)
Close the pressure equalizing valve (14.37)
Start the oil pump and raise the pressure in the hydraulic system to the
 normal value
After a settling period of about 10 minutes, carry out 5 test operations
 (open -close)
Caution: 
 Do not pressurize the operating system until the breaker has been filled with
SF6 gas.
Test operations must not be carried out without the correct SF6 gas pressure to
avoid the risk of mechanical damage.
Minimum SF6 pressure for test operations is 4.5 bar
